findings.comment: No engineer-sealed profile or section drawings with professional engineer seal are provided showing horizontal sky-to-ground clearance measurements (7 feet 6 inches minimum required) from overhead distribution primary, neutral, or secondary conductors to the biofiltration-detention pond.

No dimension lines or professional engineer-sealed calculations provided demonstrating 15-foot minimum radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors to the proposed water quality pond in all directions.
No measurements shown verifying 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance from overhead distribution facility poles to the water's edge of the proposed detention pond.

No dimension lines provided demonstrating 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance from underground distribution equipment (transformer pads, pull boxes) shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) to the edge of the proposed water quality feature.
No measurements shown verifying 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from underground electric conduits and conductors to the edge of the proposed biofiltration-detention pond.

Required profile plans and engineer-sealed section exhibits with dimension lines showing clearance verification between the proposed water quality features and all phases of overhead distribution service are not provided. Professional engineer certification demonstrating compliance with minimum clearances is absent from site plan submittal.

Permanent structures and improvements encroach into electric easements: (1) Concrete retaining wall runs along south boundary within the 5-foot Electric Easement; (2) 4-foot wide decomposed granite walkway shown within the 5-foot P.U.E. on north boundary; (3) Four-step stairway with handrails positioned at or within north boundary easement area. No structures or improvements (including hardscape, retaining walls, or stairs) are permitted within easement boundaries.

Landscaping and trees are proposed within electric easement areas on the north boundary (5-foot P.U.E.) and south boundary (5-foot Electric Easement) without required executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows trees plotted directly over overhead electric utility lines and within easement boundaries, with no notes or documentation indicating license agreement has been obtained from and filed with Austin Energy.

Landscaping and hardscape improvements shown within electric easements obstruct or restrict required 24/7 vehicular access. The 4-foot decomposed granite walkway and associated tree canopies on the north boundary within the 5-foot P.U.E., and landscaping/trees on south boundary within the electric easement, impede maintenance vehicle access required for Austin Energy personnel and equipment to distribution electric facilities.

The proposed biofiltration-detention pond retaining wall is positioned within or at the boundary of the 5-foot P.U.E. on the north boundary, obstructing required clearances and 24-hour access to electric facilities. Drainage structures and detention ponds are prohibited or must be positioned outside electric easement boundaries to maintain unimpeded access for Austin Energy maintenance.

Pond perimeter fencing shown as permanent concrete retaining wall with the northernmost edge positioned at or within the 5-foot P.U.E. on the north boundary. The retaining wall is a non-removable, permanent structure that prevents Austin Energy crew and equipment access for required maintenance. Removable wooden fences only are permitted within easements under license agreement per UCM § 1.10.10.2.

The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) indicates a 'Vault Easement' west of Building 8 and adjacent to Unit 801, but no dimension lines or measurements are provided demonstrating the required minimum 8-foot clearance in all directions from this pedestal/subsurface vault to nearby structures, landscaping, or improvements.
